title: 2013 AMC 10B Problem 23
statement: In triangle \(\triangle ABC,\) \(AB=13,\) \(BC=14,\) and \(CA=15.\) Distinct points \(D,\) \(E,\) and \(F\) lie on segments \(\overline{BC},\) \(\overline{CA},\) and \(\overline{DE},\) respectively, such that \(\overline{AD}\perp\overline{BC},\) \(\overline{DE}\perp\overline{AC},\) and \(\overline{AF}\perp\overline{BF}.\) The length of segment \(\overline{DF}\) can be written as \(\frac{m}{n},\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are relatively prime positive integers. What is \(m+n?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(BD=x\), so \(CD=14-x\). Applying the Pythagorean Theorem to right triangles \(ABD\) and \(ACD\) gives \[ 13^2-x^2=15^2-(14-x)^2. \] Thus \(BD=5\), \(CD=9\), and \(AD=12\).

This yields the following diagram:

Because \(AD\perp BC\) and \(DE\perp AC\), we have \(\angle ADE=\angle ACD\). Also, \(\angle AFB=\angle ADB=90^\circ\), so \(A,B,D,F\) are concyclic. Hence \[ \angle ABF=\angle ADF=\angle ACD. \] In right triangle \(ACD\), \(\cos(\angle ACD)=\frac35\) and \(\sin(\angle ACD)=\frac45\). Therefore, in right triangle \(ABF\), \[ \begin{aligned} BF&=13\cdot\frac35,\\ AF&=13\cdot\frac45. \end{aligned} \]

By Ptolemy’s Theorem, we get \[ \begin{aligned} &AB \cdot DF + DB \cdot AF \\ &= BF\cdot AD . \end{aligned} \] Therefore, \[ \begin{aligned} 13\cdot DF&+5\left(13\cdot\frac45\right)\\ &=12\left(13\cdot\frac35\right). \end{aligned} \]

Dividing by \(13\) gives \(DF+4=\frac{36}{5}\), so \(DF=\frac{16}{5}\). Thus \(m+n=21\), and the correct answer is B .
hints: Use the \(13\)-\(14\)-\(15\) area data to find the altitude foot
Use the cyclic quadrilateral or similar triangles to locate \(F\) on \(DE\)
